title: When does an unclosed Home Mortgage Loans application lapse and become withdrawn?
content:
# When does an unclosed Home Mortgage Loans application lapse and become withdrawn?

This policy governs Home Mortgage Loans applications that are still in applied status, meaning recorded but not yet closed. It sets when such an application ends as withdrawn.

## Policy clause

An application not closed is withdrawn once the program's funding window, counted in calendar days, has passed after the application was recorded.

## How the days are counted

- **Clock start.** The event that starts the clock is the recording of the application; the verifiable record is the application date on the bank's record of that same application.
- **Counting.** Calendar days are counted with the day after the application date as day 1.
- **Lapse point.** The application lapses when the current date is on or after the application date plus the program's funding window in days.
- **Equality.** On the day that equals the application date plus the funding window, the application has lapsed; the boundary day is included.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

The figures below use an illustrative funding window of 20 calendar days, chosen only to show the counting; it is not any program's funding window.

| Application recorded | Day 1 | Application date plus 20 days | Current date | Lapsed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 2 March | 21 March | 20 March | No, the day before the boundary |
| 1 March | 2 March | 21 March | 21 March | Yes, on the boundary day |
| 1 March | 2 March | 21 March | 5 April | Yes, after the boundary |
| 25 December | 26 December | 14 January | 14 January | Yes, on the boundary day |

## Other ways an application ends

An application also moves from applied to withdrawn status when it is denied or withdrawn. In every case the application ends without closing.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** the window runs from the first full day after the application in 24-hour periods. **Correct basis:** calendar days are counted, day 1 being the calendar day after the application date.
- **Wrong reading:** the application lapses only on the day after the boundary. **Correct basis:** it lapses on or after the application date plus the window, so the boundary day itself counts.
- **Which record decides?** The application date on the bank's record of that application, not a date the customer recalls.
